u0: This is the neutral starting point or a neutral reset point: the designated box has not yet been picked up, and no unresolved key-loss or door-opening concern is being carried forward. The mission still requires reaching the other room and picking up the named box; until the door is already open, that means moving the blocking ball, obtaining the matching key, and unlocking the door as needed. From here, losing the key while the door remains closed records a pending key-loss risk, while opening the door without such a pending loss records a pending door-opening risk. If neither happens, the agent can continue preparing; a later box pickup still succeeds even if the discouraged key-loss/door-opening combination occurred earlier and has already been recorded and cleared.
u1: The designated target box has been picked up, so the mission's required objective is satisfied and the episode ends successfully. This final point can follow either a clean run or a run in which the discouraged key-loss/door-opening combination was broken at some point; that preference is optional and never blocks completion. No further action is needed once the box is held.
u2: The matching key has been acquired and then lost while the door was still closed, and the target box has not been picked up. That loss is remembered as the key-loss side of the discouraged combination; if the door is opened from here before the box is collected, the preference is broken, progress returns to neutral, and the agent will still have to get the box. Because the box lies beyond the closed door, the door must eventually be opened, so this stage means accepting that preference slip rather than treating it as a dead end. If nothing relevant changes, the position simply waits while remembering the lost key.
u3: The door has been opened at least once, and the target box has not yet been picked up. The opening is recorded as the door-opening side of the discouraged combination; if the key is later lost while the door is closed and the box is still not held, that breaks or repeats the preference, sends progress back to neutral, and leaves the mission still to be finished. If the door is still open, the agent can head for the named box; if it has since been shut, it must be opened again before the box can be reached. Merely waiting keeps this open-door history in place and does not hurt completion.
